c.glosario.0.definicion: A script of wedge-shaped signs pressed with a stylus into soft clay. It arose in Uruk around 3300–3100 BC and was used to write Sumerian, Akkadian, Hittite and other languages until the 1st century AD.
c.glosario.1.definicion: A language isolate, with no known relationship to any other language, spoken in southern Mesopotamia. It ceased to be spoken around the beginning of the 2nd millennium BC but was kept as a learned and liturgical language.
c.glosario.2.definicion: A Semitic language of Mesopotamia, with two major dialects: Babylonian and Assyrian. It was the diplomatic language of the Near East in the 2nd millennium BC.
c.glosario.3.definicion: The literary form of Akkadian used in the 1st millennium BC and at the end of the 2nd for the canonical versions of texts such as Gilgamesh or the Enuma Elish.
c.glosario.4.definicion: A clay medium, sun-dried or baked, on which cuneiform was written. Long works were divided into several numbered tablets.
c.glosario.5.definicion: A note at the end of a tablet giving the title, the tablet number, the scribe, the owner or the date of the copy.
c.glosario.6.definicion: A small carved stone cylinder rolled over clay to leave an image in relief. It served as a signature or mark of ownership from the Uruk period onward.
c.glosario.7.definicion: A star-shaped cuneiform sign meaning 'god' or 'sky'. It is placed before the names of gods as a determinative, a marker that was not pronounced.
c.glosario.8.definicion: A sign that indicates the category of a word (god, city, wood, person...) without being pronounced.
c.glosario.9.definicion: A sign that represents a whole word, for example AMAR.UTU for Marduk, instead of syllables.
c.glosario.10.definicion: Period and dialect of Akkadian from c. 2000–1595 BC. Most of the surviving copies of Sumerian literature date from this time.
c.glosario.11.definicion: A mythical object that confers supreme authority over the universe. It appears in the myth of Anzu and in the Enuma Elish.
c.glosario.12.definicion: Serving to ward off evil or demons. Said of amulets, protective figures such as the lamassu and the apkallu, and incantations.
c.glosario.13.definicion: A Kassite or Babylonian stele that records a land grant and is decorated with symbols of the gods who guarantee it.
c.glosario.14.definicion: The base-60 number system used in Mesopotamia. The 60 minutes of the hour and the 360 degrees of the circle derive from it.
c.glosario.15.definicion: Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature: a digital edition from the University of Oxford with transliterations and translations of some 400 Sumerian literary works.
c.glosario.16.definicion: Open Richly Annotated Cuneiform Corpus: a collaborative platform that publishes annotated editions of cuneiform texts online.
c.glosario.17.definicion: The discipline that studies the languages, texts, history and cultures of the ancient Near East that used cuneiform writing.
c.glosario.18.definicion: The art of carving seals and engraved stones, and the study of their images.
a.autores.sitchin.tesis: The Anunnaki were supposedly astronauts from the planet Nibiru, with an orbit of about 3,600 years, who came to Earth some 450,000 years ago to mine gold and created human beings through genetic engineering as a labor force. The Sumerian texts would be literal chronicles of these events.
a.autores.sitchin.formacion: Born in Baku and raised in British Mandate Palestine; graduated in economics from the University of London (London School of Economics), worked as a journalist and editor in Israel and later as an executive of a shipping company in New York. He taught himself cuneiform; he had no academic training in Sumerian or Akkadian and did not publish in specialist journals.
a.autores.von-daniken.tesis: Ancient myths and monuments supposedly preserve the memory of visits by extraterrestrials whom ancient peoples took for gods. On Mesopotamia, he cites the Epic of Gilgamesh as an account of a flight and of the effects of acceleration.
a.autores.von-daniken.formacion: Swiss, with no university education; he worked as a hotel manager in Davos. He did not read ancient languages and used secondhand translations (Jason Colavito suspects a loose German adaptation of Gilgamesh).
a.autores.temple.tesis: Amphibious beings from the Sirius system supposedly visited the Earth some 5,000 years ago and passed on civilization; they would be remembered in Berossus's Oannes, the Nommo of the Dogon of Mali and other half-fish figures.
a.autores.temple.formacion: An American writer based in the United Kingdom who studied Oriental languages and Sanskrit (a biographical detail not well verified in this research). He is neither an Assyriologist nor an anthropologist; his ethnographic basis on the Dogon comes from the work of Marcel Griaule and Germaine Dieterlen.
a.autores.tsoukalos.tesis: He popularizes the ancient astronaut hypothesis on television, combining Von Däniken and Sitchin: the gods of Mesopotamia (Anunnaki) would be extraterrestrials with spacecraft and advanced technology. Jason Martell, David Childress, William Henry, M. J. Evans and Philip Coppens also appear in the series.
a.autores.tsoukalos.formacion: Tsoukalos, born in Switzerland, holds a degree in Sports Information and Communication from Ithaca College and was a bodybuilding promoter; he is publisher of the magazine Legendary Times. Neither he nor most of the series' participants have any training in Assyriology.
a.autores.alford.tesis: In 1996, following Sitchin, he argued that the gods were flesh-and-blood astronauts who genetically modified Homo erectus. He later abandoned that reading and came to interpret the myths as a personified memory of a cosmic catastrophe (a planet that exploded), criticizing Sitchin.
a.autores.alford.formacion: British, trained as an accountant and businessman; an independent author with no academic training in ancient languages. He himself admitted to having been "infatuated" with Sitchin's hypotheses.
a.autores.tellinger.tesis: The Anunnaki supposedly created humans as a slave species to mine gold in southern Africa, and thousands of stone circles in Mpumalanga (South Africa), including the so-called Adam's Calendar, would be remains of their civilization from more than 200,000 years ago.
a.autores.tellinger.formacion: South African musician and writer, founder of the Ubuntu political movement. He has no training in archaeology or Assyriology; his reading of the Sumerian texts depends on Sitchin.
a.autores.parks.tesis: A Franco-German author who presents a saga of extraterrestrial races (the Gina'abul, among them the Anunna) and maintains that Sumerian derives from a language of those beings, so he breaks Sumerian words down into syllables to extract hidden meanings. He claims to have received part of the information through visions.
a.autores.parks.formacion: No academic training in Sumerian. His method of syllabic decomposition does not correspond to standard Sumerian grammar (biographical details not well verified in this research; sources mostly from publishers and amateurs).
a.autores.lieder.tesis: She claims to receive messages from extraterrestrials from the Zeta Reticuli system through a brain implant. She announced that a Planet X would pass by the Earth in May 2003, causing a cataclysm; her followers identified it with Sitchin's Nibiru and moved the date to 2012.
a.autores.lieder.formacion: A self-described contactee and medium; no training in astronomy. David Morrison (NASA) described her as "a self-proclaimed psychic who says she channels aliens".
a.entradas.anunnaki.titulo_alternativo: The Anunnaki, "those who from heaven to Earth came"
a.entradas.anunnaki.interpretacion:
This is the axis of the whole movement. Sitchin, in The 12th Planet (1976) and the rest of the Earth Chronicles, maintains that the Anunnaki were a human-looking extraterrestrial species from Nibiru. They supposedly arrived in the Persian Gulf some 450,000 years ago, founded Eridu as their first base and organized a colony with a military hierarchy: Anu as king on Nibiru, Enlil as commander on Earth and Enki as chief scientist. Their motive would have been gold, which they needed to repair their planet's atmosphere. Sitchin also identifies them with the Nephilim of Genesis 6.

The series Ancient Aliens popularized this version from 2009 onward and expanded it: Tsoukalos speaks of "giant ships", Jason Martell of a slave race created to mine gold, and David Childress of "conical" skulls. Tellinger and Parks built their own sagas on that foundation, and Alford defended it in 1996 before abandoning it.
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.0.afirm: Sitchin: "Anunnaki" means "those who from heaven to Earth came".
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.0.repli: The term is written a-nun-na and is interpreted as "princely offspring" or "offspring of An" (the sky god). Sitchin's gloss does not correspond to any Sumerian lexicon. Heiser counted some 182 occurrences of the term in Sumerian literature, and none of them links the Anunnaki with Nibiru or with a twelfth planet.
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.0.fuent: Michael S. Heiser, sitchiniswrong.com ("Zecharia Sitchin's Errors"); Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature (Oxford)
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.1.afirm: Sitchin: the Anunnaki are the biblical Nephilim, "those who came down from on high" or "the people of the fiery rockets".
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.1.repli: Nephilim derives from Hebrew naphal, "to fall", and the form only allows "the fallen ones" (in battle or in a moral sense). Sitchin also confuses Hebrew and Aramaic forms.
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.2.afirm: Sitchin: the sign DINGIR (god) would mean "the pure ones of the blazing rockets".
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.2.repli: Fritze calls this reading "tendentious and frequently strained". DINGIR is a star-shaped sign that functions as a determinative of divinity, with the value "god" or "sky".
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.3.afirm: Ancient Aliens (episode "The Anunnaki Connection"): the cuneiform texts describe the Anunnaki "in great detail" as long-lived humanoids with giant ships, able to change shape.
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.3.repli: No cuneiform text says anything of the kind. In the sources the Anunnaki are a loosely defined group of gods (for example, the gods of heaven and of the Underworld in the Enuma Elish), not long-lived mortal beings. Colavito also points out that the series calls everything Mesopotamian "Sumerian", mixing cultures separated by millennia.
a.entradas.anunnaki.afirmaciones.3.fuent: Jason Colavito, review of Ancient Aliens S6E03, jasoncolavito.com
a.entradas.anunnaki.veredicto: The Anunnaki are a group of gods well documented in the texts; reading them as astronauts rests on etymologies that specialists do not accept.
a.entradas.nibiru.interpretacion:
According to Sitchin (The 12th Planet, 1976), the Sumerians knew of a twelfth member of the solar system (counting the Sun, the Moon and the known planets), Nibiru, with a highly elliptical orbit of about 3,600 years that takes it beyond Neptune and periodically brings it back between Mars and Jupiter. It would be the home of the Anunnaki and the "planet of Marduk" of the Enuma Elish. Its passage would have caused catastrophes such as the Flood.

From 1995, Nancy Lieder announced on ZetaTalk that a "Planet X" would pass by the Earth in 2003; her followers merged it with Sitchin's Nibiru and, after that date failed, tied it to the end of the Maya calendar in 2012. Sitchin did not endorse those predictions. Alan Alford, a former follower, abandoned the idea after studying the astronomical data.
a.entradas.nibiru.afirmaciones.0.afirmac: Sitchin: Nibiru is a planet beyond Pluto where the Anunnaki live.
a.entradas.nibiru.afirmaciones.0.replica: In Akkadian, nēberu means "crossing" or "crossing point" (of a river, for example). In astronomy it designates a point or celestial body associated with Marduk: in MUL.APIN it is usually identified with Jupiter and sometimes with Mercury. After reviewing the occurrences collected in the Chicago Assyrian Dictionary, Heiser concludes that no text places it beyond Pluto or links it with the Anunnaki.
a.entradas.nibiru.afirmaciones.0.fuente_: Michael S. Heiser, "The Myth of a Sumerian 12th Planet: Nibiru According to the Cuneiform Sources", sitchiniswrong.com; Chicago Assyrian Dictionary, s.v. nēberu
a.entradas.nibiru.afirmaciones.1.afirmac: Sitchin: Nibiru has an orbit of 3,600 years.
a.entradas.nibiru.afirmaciones.1.replica: No text gives that period. Sitchin takes it from the šar, the unit of 3,600 in the sexagesimal system used in the King List. According to astronomers, such an orbit would have a semi-major axis of about 235 AU and would be unstable: the planet would end up ejected or in another orbit.
a.entradas.nibiru.afirmaciones.1.fuente_: Summary of astronomical criticisms in the "Zecharia Sitchin" entry, Wikipedia; C. Leroy Ellenberger, 1981 article
a.entradas.nibiru.afirmaciones.2.afirmac: Lieder and her followers: Nibiru will collide with the Earth or pass close by it (May 2003, December 2012).
a.entradas.nibiru.afirmaciones.2.replica: Such a planet would be visible to the naked eye years before it arrived and would disturb the known orbits. David Morrison, of the NASA Astrobiology Institute, received nearly a thousand questions on the subject and concluded that the Nibiru hoax has "no factual basis". None of the dates came true.
a.entradas.nibiru.afirmaciones.2.fuente_: David Morrison, NASA "Ask an Astrobiologist" and 2011 video; NASA, "Beyond 2012: Why the World Won't End", 2012
a.entradas.nibiru.veredicto: Nibiru is a real Babylonian astronomical term, probably linked to Jupiter and Marduk; Sitchin's wandering planet and the announcements of catastrophe have no textual or astronomical basis.
a.entradas.sello-va243.titulo_alternativ: The VA 243 seal, a map of the solar system
a.entradas.sello-va243.interpretacion: In The 12th Planet, Sitchin reproduces an Akkadian cylinder seal from the Vorderasiatisches Museum in Berlin (inventory no. VA 243). At the upper left is a central star surrounded by eleven dots. Sitchin interprets it as the Sun surrounded by eleven bodies (planets and the Moon), that is, twelve members including Nibiru, and presents it as proof that the Sumerians knew of Uranus, Neptune, Pluto and a planet unknown to modern science, with correct relative sizes. The image became an emblem of the movement and appears frequently on Ancient Aliens.
a.entradas.sello-va243.afirmaciones.0.af: Sitchin: the central star on the seal is the Sun.
a.entradas.sello-va243.afirmaciones.0.re: On hundreds of Mesopotamian seals and monuments the Sun is depicted with four arms and wavy lines coming out of a disk, or as a disk with wavy rays. The star on VA 243 lacks those wavy lines and has six points, like the stars in this iconography (which can have 6, 7 or 8). It is therefore a star, not the Sun.
a.entradas.sello-va243.afirmaciones.0.fu: Michael S. Heiser, "The Myth of a 12th Planet in Sumerian Texts: VA 243", sitchiniswrong.com (PDF)
a.entradas.sello-va243.afirmaciones.1.af: Sitchin: the seal proves that the Sumerians knew of twelve bodies in the solar system.
a.entradas.sello-va243.afirmaciones.1.re: The seal's inscription is an ownership formula, of the type "Dubsiga; Ili-illat, your servant", and does not mention celestial bodies. The cuneiform astronomical texts (such as MUL.APIN) know only five planets visible to the naked eye, plus the Sun and the Moon. Heiser suggests that the dots may represent a star cluster or a symbol linked to a fertility deity.
a.entradas.sello-va243.afirmaciones.1.fu: Michael S. Heiser, sitchiniswrong.com; Hunger and Pingree, MUL.APIN, 1989
a.entradas.sello-va243.veredicto: For specialists, the seal shows a presentation scene before a deity with a star symbol; there is no iconographic or textual basis for reading it as a map of the solar system.
